newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Consultants to bid on Sao Paulo power sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Consultants to bid on Sao Paulo power sell-off.

text.p: Sao Paulo state will kick off its privatization process this week when consulting firms begin bidding for contracts to advise on the sale of state power firms, an official said.

"We will receive proposals from consultants, who will compete to advise us on the sale of Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL), Eletropaulo and Cesp," said Ricardo Lima, an official at the Sao Paulo state Energy Secretariat who advises investors on the state's privatization plan.
Analysts estimate the government could raise $12 billion from the sale of the utilities.

On Wednesday the state government will receive bids from firms interested in evaluating CPFL assets, while on Thursday and Friday it will receive bids from firms interested in evaluating Eletropaulo and Cesp assets, respectively, he said.
The state government will choose the winners in March. After that the consultants will have about five months to evaluate the firms' assets, Lima said.

CPFL is expected to be auctioned in August, when the state government will sell its 60.7 percent voting stake in the firm. Sao Paulo state government hopes to sell its 63.2 percent and 99.9 percent voting stake in Eletropaulo and Cesp, respectively, in September, Lima said.
Cesp is Brazil's largest power generator and Eletropaulo is South America's largest power distributor.

The state government will hold a public hearing on Jan 22 when it will present investors bid specifications to hire consultants to advise on the sale of its natural gas distributor Comgas and sell concessions to distribute gas in the state, he said.
Lima said Comgas could be auctioned by November.
